title: The Subject Is Jazz with Gilbert Seldes and Billy Taylor
summary: Writing examples for a small band each week for the NBC educational series, with guests such as Ellington and Copland.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Uh-huh. NBC Educational Series, with Gilbert Seldes, commentator. "The Subject Is Jazz," 1958.

Yes. Well, my job there was to -- incidentally, this is Billy Taylor again, with a small group, and he had Ed Thigpen, Doc Severinsen, Tony Scott on clarinet, and I forget the other one. Oh, Jimmy Cleveland. And my job was to give an example -- we had different guests every week, and my job was to do homework and write in that vein. So Seldes or the guests could make a commentary on it.

But the thing about it, to write it for a small orchestra was pretty tough, you know. Because some of those things they wanted to talk about and did talk about, were large sized outfits. Like Ellington was there. Aaron Copland. Oh, what's this other fine composer that moved -- jazz composer that moved to -- George -- he was a teacher, too. Moved to Sweden. Can't think of his name. George Russell.
Yeah. Who else? Gee, I can't remember, but I had to do the second 13 weeks. It was on for a year, you know.
